thought.text: MinIO server works perfectly. Now let me build the two Docker images (`minio/minio`, `minio/mc`) from these binaries:

reasoning_content:
The MinIO server is fully functional (health check returns 200, console is up). Next, let's build two Docker images.

For minio/minio:
- base: golang:alpine or debian bookworm-slim? The actual minio image is based on the golang build. All we need is the binary + curl for the health check + /bin/sh + the minio user (uid 1000) + /data directory.

Dockerfile:
```
FROM debian:bookworm-slim
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl ca-certificates && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
RUN groupadd -g 1000 minio-user && useradd -u 1000 -g minio-user -m minio-user
RUN mkdir -p /data && chown -R 1000:1000 /data
COPY minio /usr/bin/minio
EXPOSE 9000 9001
HEALTHCHECK CMD curl -fsS http://localhost:9000/minio/health/live >/dev/null || exit 1
USER 1000:1000
ENTRYPOINT ["minio"]
CMD ["server", "/data", "--address", ":9000", "--console-address", ":9001"]
```

The health check uses curl, and compose overrides the command with `server /data --console-address ":9001"`, so the address defaults to 9000. OK.

For minio/mc:
```
FROM debian:bookworm-slim
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl ca-certificates && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
COPY mc /usr/bin/mc
ENTRYPOINT ["mc"]
CMD ["--help"]
```

The compose's minio-init overrides the entrypoint with /bin/sh, so /bin/sh needs to exist — it does exist in debian.

The official mc image is actually alpine-based with ENTRYPOINT ["mc"]. Our compose's minio-init sets its own entrypoint ["/bin/sh","-c","..."]. No problem.

First we need to pull the debian:bookworm-slim base image. That's from Docker Hub (public) — should work just like redis.

Next, tag them:
- docker tag minio-local minio/minio:latest
- docker tag mc-local minio/mc:latest

Wait — if we tag a locally-built image as `minio/minio:latest` (the exact reference without a registry prefix), it'll be used by `docker compose` (image: minio/minio → resolves to docker.io/library? no — minio/minio has a slash but no dot in the first component, so → resolves to docker.io/minio/minio:latest). If the image exists locally with the exact reference `minio/minio:latest`, compose will use it without pulling (it only pulls when it's not local). `docker compose up --wait` doesn't force a pull by default. OK.

Let's build these.

action.command:
cd /workspace/.minio-build
cat > Dockerfile.minio <<'EOF'
FROM debian:bookworm-slim
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl ca-certificates && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
RUN groupadd -g 1000 minio-user && useradd -u 1000 -g minio-user -m -d /home/minio-user minio-user
RUN mkdir -p /data && chown -R 1000:1000 /data
COPY minio /usr/bin/minio
EXPOSE 9000 9001
USER 1000:1000
ENTRYPOINT ["minio"]
CMD ["server", "/data", "--address", ":9000", "--console-address", ":9001"]
EOF
cat > Dockerfile.mc <<'EOF'
FROM debian:bookworm-slim
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
COPY mc /usr/bin/mc
ENTRYPOINT ["mc"]
CMD ["--version"]
EOF
echo "=== pulling debian base ==="; docker pull debian:bookworm-slim 2>&1 | tail -1
echo "=== building minio/minio ==="; docker build -f Dockerfile.minio -t minio/minio:latest . 2>&1 | tail -3
echo "=== building minio/mc ==="; docker build -f Dockerfile.mc -t minio/mc:latest . 2>&1 | tail -3
docker images | grep -E "minio|debian"
